title.back: Section review: Culture, society and identity

intro.source: 10 questions about Lessons 15–19. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 10 questions about Lessons 15-19. Take your time. You can look at the lessons again and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.note: 'Góc nhìn' for 'perspective': my choice, not in KEY_TERMS. Alternatives: 'quan điểm', 'cách nhìn'. Check.
questions.0.question.source: A player sees a football shirt as part of the team. A fan sees it as a happy memory. They have different perspectives. What does perspective mean?
questions.0.question.back: A player sees a football shirt as part of a team. A fan sees it as a happy memory. They have different viewpoints. What does viewpoint mean?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: A person who makes things with their hands or tools
questions.0.options.0.text.back: The person who makes an object by hand or with tools

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. That is a maker. The player and the fan did not make the shirt. Look back at Lesson 15.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. That is the person who makes the object. The player and the fan did not make the shirt. Look at Lesson 15 again.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: The way one person sees or thinks about something
questions.0.options.1.text.back: The way a person looks at or thinks about something

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. A perspective is the way one person sees something. The player and the fan see the same shirt in different ways.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. A viewpoint is the way a person looks at something. The player and the fan look at the same shirt in different ways.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: A picture or shape that stands for an idea
questions.0.options.2.text.back: A picture or shape that stands for an idea

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. That is a symbol. Here, each person sees the shirt in their own way. Look back at Lesson 15.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. That is a symbol. Here, each person looks at the shirt in their own way. Look at Lesson 15 again.

questions.1.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks.

questions.1.stimulus.items.0.source: The seller says it is for playing music at events.
questions.1.stimulus.items.0.back: The seller says it is used to play music at events.

questions.1.stimulus.items.1.source: The owner says it reminds her of the day she joined a music club.
questions.1.stimulus.items.1.back: The owner says it reminds her of the day she joined a music club.

questions.1.stimulus.items.2.note: 'Mẫu hình' for 'pattern' in a drum context is ambiguous: it could be a rhythm or a design. The English is also ambiguous. Native speaker please check that the word works for a drum 'pattern' that is taught and also 'means' something. | Review: English 'the pattern' on a drum taught by a drummer; 'mẫu hình' (glossary: trend/pattern) is abstract and odd for a drum. 'nhịp trống' assumes a rhythm; if the English meant a painted design, 'họa tiết' would be right. Native reviewer to confirm. [Reviewer changed: mẫu hình này → nhịp trống này (also in options.0.text, options.0.feedback, options.2.feedback)]
questions.1.stimulus.items.2.source: The maker says an older drummer taught her the pattern.
questions.1.stimulus.items.2.back: The maker says an older drummer taught her this pattern.

questions.1.question.source: A museum wants a label for this drum. Which label is best, based on Lesson 15?
questions.1.question.back: A museum wants a label for this drum. Based on Lesson 15, which label is best?

questions.1.options.0.text.note: A wrong option, kept clearly wrong because no note says what the pattern means. Check it does not sound like it might be correct.
questions.1.options.0.text.source: The pattern is a symbol of the whole town and all its people.
questions.1.options.0.text.back: This pattern is a symbol of the whole town and everyone in it.

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. No note says what the pattern means. A good label does not guess. Look back at Lesson 15.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. No note says what this pattern means. A good label does not guess. Look at Lesson 15 again.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: It is just an everyday drum. It has no other meaning for anyone.
questions.1.options.1.text.back: This is just an ordinary drum. It has no other meaning for anyone.

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The notes show that the drum also holds a memory and a skill. Look back at Lesson 15.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The notes show the drum holds a memory and a skill. Look at Lesson 15 again.

questions.1.options.2.text.note: Correct option (label for the drum). It is the longest of the three because the English is; I kept the wrong options close in length so it does not stand out. Check the label still sounds like a real museum label. | Review: Correct label is the longest option (as in English, but slightly more so in Vietnamese). Consider shortening or lengthening others.
questions.1.options.2.text.source: For music. It holds a memory for its owner and a skill for its maker.
questions.1.options.2.text.back: Used to play music. It holds a memory of the owner and a skill of the person who made it.

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. This label uses what the seller, the owner and the maker say. It does not guess what the pattern means.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. This label uses what the seller, the owner and the maker said. It does not guess what the pattern means.

questions.2.question.note: 'Hillside Learning Centre' is an invented place: written 'Trung tâm học tập Hillside' (translated 'Learning Centre', kept 'Hillside'). Check that it matches Lesson 16. 'Ngôn ngữ ký hiệu' for sign language.
questions.2.question.source: At Hillside Learning Centre, a volunteer talks about the food notice. Some visitors read the notice in English. Others use the pictures, sign language or help from a friend. What does this show?
questions.2.question.back: At the Hillside learning centre, a volunteer talks about a food-handout notice. Some guests read the notice in English. Others use pictures, sign language or ask a friend to help. What does this show?

questions.2.options.0.text.note: Shortened to keep the correct option from being the longest; check the meaning ('one message understood in several ways') is preserved.
questions.2.options.0.text.source: People can understand one message in different ways.
questions.2.options.0.text.back: People understand a message in many ways.

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Visitors use words, pictures, sign language or a friend's help. They all get the same message in different ways.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. Guests use words, pictures, sign language or ask a friend for help. All get the same message in different ways.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: Most visitors do not want to read the notice.
questions.2.options.1.text.back: Most guests do not want to read that notice.

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The visitors do want the message. They use different ways to understand it. Look back at Lesson 16.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The guests really want to know the message. They use different ways to understand it. Look at Lesson 16 again.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: Only people who read English can come to the centre.
questions.2.options.2.text.back: Only people who can read English come to the centre.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The notice says the food is for everyone. Many visitors understand it without reading English. Look back at Lesson 16.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The notice says food is for everyone. Many guests understood it without reading English. Look at Lesson 16 again.

questions.3.question.note: Core idea: no language is better than another. Respectful-language review: please check this is stated kindly and without ranking.
questions.3.question.source: Lesson 16 says that no language is better than another. What reason does it give?
questions.3.question.back: Lesson 16 says no language is better than another. What reason does the lesson give?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: All languages use the very same words for things.
questions.3.options.0.text.back: All languages use exactly the same words for everything.

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Languages have different words, and they borrow words from each other. Look back at Lesson 16.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Languages have different words, and they borrow words from each other. Look at Lesson 16 again.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: Each language is spoken by the same number of people.
questions.3.options.1.text.back: Every language has an equal number of speakers.

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The lesson does not count speakers. It talks about what each language holds. Look back at Lesson 16.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The lesson does not count speakers. It is about what each language keeps. Look at Lesson 16 again.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: Each one holds the stories of its speakers.
questions.3.options.2.text.back: Each language keeps the stories of its speakers.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.note: Check 'lưu giữ' (hold/keep) is natural for 'holds the stories of its speakers'.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Every language holds the knowledge and stories of its speakers. So no language is the best.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. Each language keeps the knowledge and stories of the people who speak it. So no language is the best.

questions.4.question.note: 'Sự truyền lại' for transmission per KEY_TERMS. 'Lễ mừng' for 'celebration': my choice. 'Mục đích' for 'purpose'.
questions.4.question.source: In a made-up village, older weavers show young people how to make baskets. Later, the young people will teach others. Which word from Lesson 17 names this?
questions.4.question.back: In a made-up village, older basket weavers show young people how to make baskets. Later, the young people will teach others. Which word from Lesson 17 names this?

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A celebration marks a special day with others. Here, older people pass a skill to younger people. Look back at Lesson 17.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A celebration marks a special day with many people. Here, older people pass a skill to young people. Look at Lesson 17 again.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Transmission means passing knowledge or skills from one person to another. The weavers pass on their skill.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. Passing down means moving knowledge or skill from one person to another. The weavers pass down their skill.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A purpose is the reason why something is done. Here, older people pass a skill to younger people. Look back at Lesson 17.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A purpose is the reason people do something. Here, older people pass a skill to young people. Look at Lesson 17 again.

questions.5.question.source: What does Lesson 17 say about traditions that change?
questions.5.question.back: What does Lesson 17 say about traditions that change?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: A tradition can change and still keep its purpose.
questions.5.options.0.text.back: A tradition can change and still keep its purpose.

questions.5.options.0.feedback.note: Community meal: the Vietnamese Lesson 17 may use a different phrase for 'community meal'. Check.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The community meal starts earlier and adds new dishes. It still helps people meet, teach and welcome others.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. A community meal starts earlier and adds new dishes. It still helps people meet, teach each other and welcome others.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: A tradition ends as soon as people change it.
questions.5.options.1.text.back: A tradition ends as soon as people change it.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. People adapt traditions to fit new times, and the meal still goes on. Look back at Lesson 17.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. People adjust traditions to fit new times, and the meal continues. Look at Lesson 17 again.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Only the very oldest way of doing it is the right way.
questions.5.options.2.text.back: Only the oldest way is the right way.

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Traditions are not frozen in the past. People adapt them to fit new times. Look back at Lesson 17.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Traditions are not frozen in the past. People adjust them to fit new times. Look at Lesson 17 again.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.note: Review: 'bị đóng băng trong quá khứ' literal metaphor (frozen); understandable, 'không đứng yên' would be plainer.

questions.6.question.note: Real places: 'Algeria' (some Vietnamese texts: 'An-giê-ri'), 'Trung Quốc', 'Vanuatu'. Reviewer decides the usual spelling of Algeria.
questions.6.question.source: Lesson 18 gives three examples: rock art in Algeria, a painted scroll in China and sand drawings in Vanuatu. What do they all show?
questions.6.question.back: Lesson 18 gives three examples: rock paintings in Algeria, a painted scroll in China and sand drawings in Vanuatu. What do all three show together?

questions.6.options.0.text.source: Art from long ago is always about animals.
questions.6.options.0.text.back: Old art is always about animals.

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The rock art shows animals, but the scroll shows a busy city full of people. Look back at Lesson 18.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The rock paintings include animals, but the scroll paints a busy city full of people. Look at Lesson 18 again.

questions.6.options.1.text.source: People around the world tell stories with art.
questions.6.options.1.text.back: People all over the world tell stories through art.

questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The three examples come from different parts of the world. In each place, people use art to tell stories and keep knowledge.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. The three examples come from different places in the world. In each place, people use art to tell stories and keep knowledge.

questions.6.options.2.text.source: Only one part of the world tells stories with art.
questions.6.options.2.text.back: Only one place in the world tells stories through art.

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The three examples come from three different places. People all over the world tell stories with art. Look back at Lesson 18.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The three examples come from three different places. People everywhere in the world tell stories through art. Look at Lesson 18 again.

questions.7.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks.

questions.7.stimulus.body.note: Curly quotes kept. 'Chúng ta cùng lớn lên' for 'We grow together'; check it matches the mural text in Lesson 18 if shown there.
questions.7.stimulus.body.source: A mural is a big painting on a wall. This one is on the wall of a made-up school. It shows a tall tree with long roots. Children of different heights hold hands around the tree. At the top are the words “We grow together”.
questions.7.stimulus.body.back: A mural is a large painting on a wall. This one is on the wall of a made-up school. It shows a tall tree with long roots. Children of different heights hold hands around the tree. Above is the text "We grow together".

questions.7.question.note: 'Diễn giải' for 'interpretation' (Lesson 18 glossary) and 'quan sát' for 'observation'. Check the distinction is clear to a child.
questions.7.question.source: Which sentence is an interpretation of the mural?
questions.7.question.back: Which sentence is an interpretation of the mural?

questions.7.options.0.text.source: The mural may be about working as a team.
questions.7.options.0.text.back: The mural may be about working as a team.

questions.7.options.0.feedback.note: The English says 'may shows you are careful'; kept as 'từ “có thể” cho thấy bạn thận trọng'. Check tone.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. This is an idea about what the mural means. The joined hands and the words support it, and “may” shows you are careful.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. This is an idea about the meaning of the picture. The held hands and the text support this idea, and the word "may" shows you are careful.

questions.7.options.1.text.source: Children hold hands around a tall tree.
questions.7.options.1.text.back: Children hold hands around a tall tree.

questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. This is an observation. Anyone can check it by looking at the mural. Look back at Lesson 18.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. This is an observation. Anyone can check by looking at the picture. Look at Lesson 18 again.

questions.7.options.2.text.source: The words at the top say “We grow together”.
questions.7.options.2.text.back: The text above says "We grow together".

questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. This is an observation. Anyone can read the words on the wall. Look back at Lesson 18.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This is an observation. Anyone can read the text on the wall. Look at Lesson 18 again.

questions.8.question.note: 'Rào cản' for barrier (KEY_TERMS). The problem is a language barrier; check it is told without blame.
questions.8.question.source: A made-up art club writes its meeting times in only one language. Some members cannot read that language, so they miss meetings. Which word from Lesson 19 names this problem?
questions.8.question.back: A made-up art club writes meeting times in only one language. Some members cannot read that language, so they miss meetings. Which word from Lesson 19 names this problem?

questions.8.options.0.feedback.note: 'Quyền chủ động' for agency per KEY_TERMS. Lesson 19 on belonging is sensitive; the check only asks about ideas in the reading. Please check the wording.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Agency is the power to make choices and act. This problem makes it hard to take part. Look back at Lesson 19.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Agency is the power to choose and act for yourself. This problem makes it hard to take part. Look at Lesson 19 again.

questions.8.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. An opinion is what a person thinks about something. This problem makes it hard to take part. Look back at Lesson 19.
questions.8.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. An opinion is what a person thinks about something. This problem makes it hard to take part. Look at Lesson 19 again.

questions.8.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. A barrier makes it harder for someone to take part. The club could share its times in more than one way.
questions.8.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. A barrier makes it harder for someone to take part. The club could share meeting times in several ways.

questions.9.question.note: Belonging = 'cảm giác thuộc về' (KEY_TERMS). Sensitive lesson (belonging): please check the wording of all three options.
questions.9.question.source: What does Lesson 19 say a group can do so that more people feel they belong?
questions.9.question.back: Lesson 19 says what a group can do so that more people feel they belong?

questions.9.options.0.text.source: Ask new members to share private things
questions.9.options.0.text.back: Ask new members to tell private stories

questions.9.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The lesson says nobody should have to share private things to belong. Look back at Lesson 19.
questions.9.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The lesson says no one has to share private stories to belong. Look at Lesson 19 again.

questions.9.options.1.text.source: Change the way the group works

questions.9.options.1.feedback.note: 'Quy tắc nói lần lượt từng người' for 'turn-taking rules': check it is natural.
questions.9.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The club does not need to change its members. It can change how it works, for example with turn-taking rules.
questions.9.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. The club does not need to change its members. It can change how it works, for example with rules for taking turns to speak.

questions.9.options.2.text.source: Ask members to act like everyone else
questions.9.options.2.text.back: Ask members to behave like everyone else

questions.9.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The lesson says a group should change how it works, not change its members. Look back at Lesson 19.
questions.9.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The lesson says a group should change how it works, not change its members. Look at Lesson 19 again.

results.high.note: Check the warmth and that 'giúp người khác cảm thấy mình thuộc về' reads naturally.
results.high.source: Well done. You know a lot about how people share meaning and help others belong.
results.high.back: Well done. You know a lot about how people share meaning and help others feel they belong.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good. You answered many correctly. Look at the lessons again for the ones not right, and try again if you like.
results.middle.note: Review: Unnatural preposition. [Reviewer changed: cho những câu chưa đúng → về những câu bạn chưa làm đúng]

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 15–19, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Look at Lessons 15-19 again then try again. You can take as much time as you like.
